page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-16 is a memory-dense instance type configured with an x86_64 Intel processor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. Hardware acceleration features include Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) alongside extensive AVX-512 instructions such as VNNI and BF16. Cache hierarchy is provisioned with 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache.

The instance delivers 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk needs. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included. In addition, the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network routing or elastic addressing for direct external access.

Benchmark measurements position the n4-highmem-16 within the middle 50 percent across standard metrics. In memory throughput tests, the system records 1,084.69 GB/sec for small cached reads, 115.64 GB/sec for large uncached reads, and 66.19 GB/sec for large writes. In workload-specific tests, the server processes 17.18 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database operations score of 7,313.73. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench ratings reach 1,836.0 and 10,971.0 respectively. CPU-based inference evaluates at 90.56 prompt tokens per second and 11.28 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and modern vector execution extensions, the n4-highmem-16 provides solid resource density for RAM-dependent workloads. Tradeoffs include reliance on external persistent disks and lack of GPU acceleration. The server fits database engines, distributed in-memory caching nodes, batch ETL pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial memory residency.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-16 is a memory-dense virtual machine within the general-purpose compute family, engineered with an x86_64 Intel processor. It delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, paired with 128 GB of system memory at an allocation ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, necessitating external network storage for persistent data. Across standardized benchmarks, the server demonstrates consistent middle-tier performance, achieving 17.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 115.64 GB/s large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Its architectural balance of substantial memory capacity and vectorized instruction execution renders it effective for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caching tiers, relational database instances, data processing pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.
